provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The legends are runs of at least 2 non-background cells along the strip axis on a grid edge. Each lone pixel is replaced by a translated copy of the legend that contains its colour. The copy is aligned so that the matching legend cell lands on the pixel, and cells beyond the grid are clipped. The D4 transform applies to inputs and outputs alike, so the stamp is a pure translation of the legend exactly as it appears. Reflections therefore need no reversing logic: only the axis changes. For d4%4 in {1,3} the legends become vertical runs on the left or right column and stamps slide along columns. Otherwise legends are horizontal and stamps slide along rows. The background is the constant palette[0]. The emitted code works directly in visible coordinates with explicit row or column loops. It does not rotate or transpose the grid. One generator edge case is handled: two maximal 6-long legends can merge on a 12-long edge, and that merged full-edge run is split in half.
draft_notes.limitations: This has not been tested. The merged-legend split assumes the generator's maximum legend length of 6. If a pixel colour appears in several legends, the first legend found wins, but the generator rejects such scenes. Pixels whose colour is in no legend are left unchanged.
